Dr. Haag is a very nice guy, and does his best to be engaging and interesting with material that is not necessarily that cool. Personally, I don't see the value in this class especially since a lot of it is just detailed AP Biology and concepts that most people should already be familiar with, just in a really detailed format. If you want this class as transfer credit, it counts as general bio 2 in most other universities, which emphasizes what I said before. Whenever Dr. Haag does what he calls "tours of organisms" the class gets confusing since we don't know what we're supposed to be taking notes on and what we actually have to know, since he just seems to be presenting basically fun facts of each organism. For these tours, I would recommend that you take notes on the key concepts that make them different from other organisms instead of memorizing every single feature of each organism, since test questions won't ask you about random specific information, rather they will ask you about how it is relevant and why it matters.

All that being said, however, the class itself is not difficult provided you are willing to put in more than the bare minimum amount of effort to get by, which can be said for all biology classes at any university. The class is intuition-based provided you have memorized the key concepts needed to be able to use intuition. As a study technique, I HIGHLY recommend reviewing for exams through the GSS sessions and going through every lecture and making sure you can understand each slide and put it in your own words. There are no past exams, at least not for our semester, so the GSS leader makes practice exam questions and summarizes each of the lectures, so definitely go to those. He allows you to drop a test at the end of the semester (even though I probably won't need to) which can be hugely impactful for people that failed the first test and needed to get the hang of things and the way the class is taught. There are 4 units and 1 exam per unit, the exams are fair in length and difficulty. He even adjusts the length and difficulty of exams based on performance of his students on previous exams. Personally, I think Dr. Haag is doing a good job at teaching all this material in a way that keeps us interested and engaged. Whenever he geeks out over concepts, it makes the class a lot more interesting and even though we don't always get through the material in lecture, part of the responsibility of reviewing lecture notes afterwards lays on us students. But, I will say that having a class longer than 50 minutes would probably be better so that we can actually fully get through the material and not have to rush through parts of the lecture just to finish on time.

Dr. Haag is very responsive to emails and is very helpful as long as you are willing to take initiative and reach out to him. Overall, pretty good class as long as you put in the effort, good professor, and great person.

Dr Haag does the best he can with this terrible course. I would like to give him a poor review, but truly I think the course is the problem and not the professor. I received over a 96% average in both 161 and 171, and I am currently hoping to end with a B- in this class (207). The material covered is literally all over the place, one days information usually has nothing to do with the next. This makes it hard to retain small details and study because the topics contained on one single test can be so vastly different from each other (hard to study fungi and kidneys at the same time..). Personally, I recommend just staying away from this course. It's way too much random information and minuscule details thrown into one course. That being said, If you do need to take it for a major requirement, Haag is not a bad choice. He truly wants his students to do well and he adjusts each exam according to performance on the last exam. The averages of our exams have all been around C-, increasing with each exam. He also recently adjusted the exams so that a "cheat sheet" can be used, which is very considerate of him but it only boosted the average exam grade about 5 percent because again, the material is just so all over the place. Just be prepared to have an overwhelming amount of material covered, regardless of the professor. Take advantage of how helpful and caring Dr Haag is by asking questions and asking for help, there's also GSS sessions that are very helpful.

If I could go past 5 stars, I would. He may be one of the most understanding, kind, and humorous professors I have had. He is extremely organized, his page is easy to follow, and he is so aware of the difficulty of the class. He provides his students with literally everything you will need to succeed. We have homeworks that are graded on effort, GAE quizzes and concept checks that are sometimes directly questions that are put on the exam, and he allows a cheat sheet during exams. You really can't ask for anything more from a professor, let alone a biology/STEM prof. He is amazing and I wish I could take more classes with him!

Best professor for BSCI207. He is the most understanding and flexible professor there is. My friend has the other professor for this class and failed. There’s a lot of assignments to help boost your grade. One exam gets dropped. He has concept checks after every lecture to help ensure you understand the material. He allows cheat sheets for exams with equations etc. He is also kind and funny. He has a cute dog. He makes class fun and there’s a lot of hands on activities. 10/10 recommend.

I would agree with all the other 5 star reviews, this man deserves nothing less than a 5/5 on any teacher rating platform. He's literally so understanding and tries to make the loads of information as manageable as possible. He's funny and will tell you the crazy things about his life and he is very accessible outside of class. Cannot stress this enough, TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN. I would write more about what his grading is like but I'm too lazy, just look at the review from 12/01/2021 for a breakdown.

He is a really nice guy, but this course is not it. The material literally does not correlate with anything. One lecture we are talking about the kidney and the next class we are talking about evolutionary trends of bacteria. It made studying really hard because we had to remember every single detail. His tests are also really hard as well - but you eventually become better at taking them. Also, I don't think he curves, so there is that. Also, Dr.Haag is very enthusiastic about his work and all that he goes on tangents that make no sense and it's hard to tell what his tangent is and what the material is. Another thing that annoyed me so much is that the lecture slides for one lecture are about 50 slides. He takes 40 minutes going through 10-15 slides and then rushes the last 35-40 slides. It was really frustrating since we were still held accountable to know all of the material that he just rushed through. 

Overall, nice guy but terrible course - avoid at all costs.

I feel that he is a nice guy, but is awful at lecturing. He always plans to get through a 30-40 ppt slide in 50 mins when we only end up actually getting through about 15 of the slides (then he expects us to just know the rest for the test). Sometimes he will see that we have 5 minutes left in class and 20 more slides to get through, so he'll quickly flip through the last slides. Not only that but he is just all over the place, the slides most times are disorganized and he will talk about the least important thing for 10 minutes. His exams are so hard and he purposely tries to make the questions difficult. The averages were 50-60 range constantly, even when he let us use an 8x11 page front and back for the test. Also we had exam 4, 5 days before the final....

Would NOTTTTTT recommend him to anyone

Dr. Fletcher is seriously the best I love him so much. The material in this course can be very difficult as its a very in depth explanation of many concepts, but Dr. Fletcher gives you all the tools to succeed. For every exam he allowed an entire sheet of paper for cheat sheet notes which was very helpful. He's super understanding and knows exactly what he's talking about and how to explain it. Seriously take him for any class you can, you won't regret it.

Dr. Fletcher was a real highlight for me during my time at UMD. His class style is clear and engaging, making taking on such large chunks of information very doable. Learning expectations were clear and success in his class is viable given some effort. Outstanding professor and I would recommend him to anyone.

Dr.Haag is a super nice guy. He is very understanding and tries to make things as interesting as possible. However, the class SUCKS. BSCI207 is one of the worst classes I've ever taken and I would avoid it at all costs unless you need it for a prerequisite (like I did). The material is super boring, doesn't connect from one lecture to another, and is a jumble of things you will learn in other bio, physics, chem, and plant science classes. Dr.Haag's exams are hard to understand and are always looking for more than just memorization. Because of the type of material, it's super difficult to know what they're looking for. The TAs also aren't much help so you're kind of screwed. ALSO : 4 MIDTERMS AND A FINAL, MIDTERM 4 WAS ON THE MONDAY OF EXAM WEEK AND THE FINAL WAS ON THAT SATURDAY. Avoid at all costs!!!

I loved loved loved Dr. Fletcher! He gave you all the resources you needed to pass and didn't make his class more difficult than it needed to be. Everything connected with each other, there wasn't any busy work. The work load was absolutely fine, and the entire class was graded on (pretty much) completion except for the exams.

Fletcher is a great professor who frankly made 207 a very easy class to get a good grade in. Lectures were easy to follow, and he also provided an additional resource that was kind of like an online 207 textbook that could be helpful sometimes. The work load was not heavy at all. Following every lecture would be a quick 2 point concept check which you get 3 attempts on, and every couple weeks there would be a homework assignment that was usually pretty challenging, but they were really just graded for effort, not accuracy. There would also be these in-class group assignments (GAEs) every other week which were probably the most annoying part of the class; we had to watch a lecture video and complete a quiz in preparation for it, and the assignment itself was done on one piece of paper for the whole group of 5 or 6 people, meaning not everyone really got to see what was going on. But again, these were only graded for completion so it wasn't much of an issue.
There were 3 midterm exams which weren't that tough, considering we could make a one-sided cheat sheet paper to cram all our notes on. Same goes for the final, but the cheat sheet could actually be two-sided. He also dropped our lowest midterm grade, as well as the lowest grade in every assignment category. And there were some small extra credit questions on the exams too, so as long as you made a good cheat sheet, getting an A on them was not much of a challenge.
Overall, Fletcher is a nice guy who is very approachable and passionate, and has a cute dog.

Dr. Fletcher might be the best teacher in all of UMD. I took his class Tuesdays and Thursdays, and since he was used to having MWF lectures the class pace was a little fast, but he is such a fantastic lecturer it didn't make class any more difficult. He posts lectures for review, too! He drops the lowest assignments and test grades. There are three tests and a final, but he makes it SO EASY to review for tests. The work isn't too difficult (and if you don't understand it, there were three TAs, two GSS leaders, and Fletcher himself to help) and the work is super helpful for studying. Textbooks are not necessary, but they are helpful. If you take the class seriously and make sure you understand most of the content, it is very easy to get an A. TAKE THIS PROF!!!

Dr. Fletcher is a great professor. His assignments were pretty easy and you could go to his office hours where he's happy to answer any questions on the homework and basically gives you the answer. All of his assignments were very helpful in understanding the material. I will say there is a lot of material covered in this class and most of the questions on the exam are straight memorization and a few conceptual. I found the exams to be challenging but Dr. Fletcher is such an amazing professor so if you have any questions at all he'll be happy to help and explain things thoroughly. He also drops the lowest assignment and lowest test so if you're happy with your grade you don't need to take the last exam. Overall I would definitely recommend Fletcher for BSCI207 as it is a challenging class but he makes it as easy as possible.

Nick is a really fun and interesting lecturer. He encourages students to talk to each other and has weekly group activities. All of his lectures are on panopto with subtitles so if you miss something during class or couldn't hear something he said it isn't a problem. You can also bring a formula sheet to exams and write on it which is pretty great. If you take any other prof 4 207 you are making a mistake.

Dr. Fletcher is a super easy-going and overall kind professor who implements a lot of grading policies that are super beneficial for his students. With three classes per week, generally two of them are lectures and the other is a Group Active Engagement Session (GAE) that allows you to work with classmates on a worksheet, which is graded for completion. It's a great way to make a big class feel smaller. Before the GAEs, you have to do prep work and then take a quiz, which you only get one try on.

After every class, you have a 1 point concept check to take, which is usually 3-5 questions, and you have three tries to get 100%. These are also easy ways to get points since you can go look back at the lecture slides and your notes.

Dr. Fletcher also assigns homework approximately every two weeks that are graded on effort. They're usually not too hard. 
In regards to all of the assignments listed above, some of your worst scores get dropped since there are so many of them. So hypothetically, you could not do some of them and be completely fine since they'd be dropped.
The exams are not too too hard if you study, but if you don't, I can bet they're difficult. This class builds off a lot of previous bio classes, so having prior knowledge can help you out a lot. Dr. Fletcher allows you to bring an equation sheet that serves as a cheat sheet that you can write on for every exam. Then, he drops your worst exam grade out of three. The only bad thing about this is that I don't think there's a curve at the end of the class since one gets dropped and the class average is a C on most exams. So, you really just need to study and get good exam grades to get an overall good grade in the class because you can't rely on a curve. 
The main reason I give Dr. Fletcher 4 stars instead of 5 is because I think his lectures can get a little boring. Some of the content of this class is interesting, and Dr. Fletcher's passion does make it more interesting, but some lectures are just really hard to sit through when it's just him talking. I think it would be more engaging if some videos or animations were shown so students could see the biological processes in action.
Overall, I highly recommend Fletcher for BSCI207. I don't think you can find a better professor for it.

Nick is an engaging lecturer and is great at helping freshmen make the transition to college. He previously taught at MC so I think he has a lot of understanding regarding the difficult transition that freshmen have to make which is important for teaching 100 and 200 levels. I took 207 as a junior due to procrastination and it almost felt “too nice”. However, you are expected to stay on top of things in this class. There will usually be either one HW or one GAE (group activity) every week and there will be a concept check after every lecture. Be aware of this and always do your work. You do not want to lose easy points in this class!

Fletcher's a good professor but I personally don't really like his class. He goes really into depth with everything, but a lot of the time its just way too much talking. My lectures were only 50 minutes long but they are packeddd with information and its kind of overwhelming. It's very very useful to have cheat sheets for the exams because it's usually a lot of material. Its easy to do well in this class as long as you are prepared for each exam. The homeworks and GAE's are all graded for completion and you have a lot of opportunities to bring your grade up with the online quizzes. He gives you 3 attempts for the concept quizzes after every lecture, but just one for the GAE quizzes before the GAE to make sure you watched the GAE lecture and  material beforehand. He also drops the lowest exam, quiz, and homework. He's a really nice, engaging, and easy-going lecturer, but this class just wasn't for me. I do recommend him though.

Very nice professor! Lectures are very easy to understand if you pay attention. She records her lectures and posts her slides so that students can look back on whatever we missed, which is really helpful for when we review for exams. She had 3 exams and dropped the lowest one, so she keeps the best 2 exams. For exams, she lets us have a cheat sheet which is really helpful because it forces us to actually review the material. For the first 2 exams, she gave us opportunity to bring the score up by a couple of points. I always went to office hours and she would always be very helpful and breakdown anything I was confused about. She's probably my favorite professor!

Dr. Fletcher is great. I can only say positive things about him. He’s always smiling and you can tell he cares about what he is teaching which makes his lectures that much more interesting. He does everything in his power to make getting a good grade easy. Everything is completion other than the exams, you can drop the lowest midterm, and you can have a cheat sheet on each exam.

Dr. Fletcher is the nicest professor for 207. This course has a lot of content that is straight memorization but he lets you use cheat sheets and gives you plenty of resources to study from. After each lecture there are concept check quizzes which are questions that always end up on the midterms and the final. Attend office hours if you want answers to the exam study guides, or lecture content. He makes the classes entertaining and interactive, which is so different from other professors. He also records lectures so if you miss a few it's not a big deal. As long as you study in advance of the exams this class will be easy.

Fletcher is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about his students and what he's teaching. He's always really clear on what is expected on assignments and exams, and he grades leniently. This course, in general, is super content heavy, so definitely make sure to watch all of the lectures, as each 50 minute lecture has loads of content. He is really great at explaining each concept. The fact that he allows a cheat sheet on his exams definitely helps, and his exams accurately reflect his exam guides, homework, and GAEs. As long as you do all of the work and keep up on lectures, you will be fine. I would highly recommend taking Fletcher.

Dr. Fletcher is a great professor! He records all his lectures, drops the lowest grade in each category, and has very fair exams. The questions are always straight forward and I never felt like there was a question that we never covered. He also sometimes cracks jokes or asks you to discuss with your classmates during lecture which keeps you engaged. One complaint though is that he sometimes talks fast and covers a LOT of information in one lecture. It can be really hard to keep up and can get boring at times if you're not interested in the topics. However, I feel like the fact that he records lectures compensate for this since you can always catch up on information you missed later. Overall, nice guy and I would for sure recommend him for 207.

Like everyone says, she’s a kind and sincere professor. I just feel the lectures are her reading off the 50 or so slides where we don’t even have time to write much of anything down. Each lecture is pretty loosely related to each other so it doesn’t really matter too much if you skip one because you can watch the recording. I felt she was an alright prof and attribute most of my success to the cheat sheet for exams and just reviewing lecture recordings because I skipped a decent amount of lectures.

Fletcher is the nicest guy you'll ever meet; he makes the class environment super welcoming towards new students and won't hesitate to help you. However, I found his exams kinda difficult; they are very detail-oriented, and while it holds true that everything comes off of his slideshows, his slideshows are each about 75 slides long, and there's around 10 slideshows per unit. It's a lot of content to cover. If I could retake the course, I'd start reviewing information earlier before exams because a lot of it is memory based. 
I also think his lectures are more on the ramble-y side, but he records them, so you don't have to attend if you don't want to. Overall, great and approachable guy!

I loved Dr. Karen. She is the sweetest professor I've had so far and she clearly cares about what she's teaching. The only reason I took off a star is because classes are boring and she kinda just reads from the slide. I also had a hard time telling what to study or telling how specific the exams would get about the content. But other than that it was chill. There are concept checks that are ungraded practice DO THEM literally like 30% of the first exam multiple choice I already knew because I did the checks. Could have gotten an A if I studied more and went to class :/

Great professor! He really cares about all of his students and listens to any concerns we have about exams, homework, due dates, etc. The class is definitely hard, but the work and exams are fair. you should definitely go to lecture, he posts the slides on canvas, but he talks about them and adds a lot more info that isn’t on the power point. He adds in humor which keeps the class engaging and fun.

Dr. Carleton is one of the best teachers I have had. She broke down the content into well-organized lectures. She was very clear with what will be tested and made the memorization-heavy content digestible. She allowed us to make and have a cheat sheet which was a lifesaver. DO THE CONCEPT CHECKS! The concept checks are going to be very helpful. She genuinely is a good teacher and wants you to do well.

his class was the most boring class i've ever had to take. he would always read straight from the slides in a monotonous tone. that being said, he's accommodating and flexible and his exams are very fair.

Would not recommend him for bsci207. Pls take someone else if u can. He's pretty monotone. His exams and quizzes are unnecessarily hard. Hw are annoying because T.A take a lot of points off. The only good thing is he drops the lowest midterm or down weight the finals.

Really good lecturer and overall an extremely nice person. Lecture slides are posted but I highly recommend attending lectures because anything he emphasizes almost always shows up on tests. If you really just pay attention to what he is saying you can get an A. Exams are extremely fair and similar to the practice questions he posts. The quizzes always have one hard question. I got a 4/5 on almost every quiz. Homeworks are easy and graded lightly. Overall he is extremely nice he was consistently extending quiz and homework deadlines to help people out.

Dr. Shapiro is super nice and fun! I don't see why other reviewers called him boring. He really cares about these topics (especially scaling, so be sure to study that). His lectures are super super dense, which can be tiring, but he makes jokes to help you get through them. 
He is very open to criticism. One of my classmates informed him that he lectured too fast, and by the next class it was fixed. He assigned a super hard homework, which received complaints, and he apologized. It did not happen again. You definitely don't see this type of behavior often from professors. When a class average on an exam was too low (I don't know exactly what percent that was) he would scale it up a couple points. Also, an entire exam was dropped, and there were a couple points of extra credit given during the semester.
There are small multiple choice quizzes given on each topic, and 5 homework assignments. He extended the deadline on a lot of our quizzes, but I would not expect that to occur as often in the future.
The exams are a bit tough because the material is a bit tough. But, they're fair, especially given that one of the 3 exams was dropped. Overall, I would take a class with Dr. Shapiro again. I have not had many STEM professors that care about their students as much as he does.
Do not take him for bsci207. Exams are way harder than other profs
He's very nice and he's a great lecturer!

Literally the best professor I have ever had. He cares about his students so much, and wants all of us to do well in his class. I hope to have him again for BSCI370 because he makes me enjoy the class, and his teaching style makes everyone enjoy coming to lecture. If you have a chance to take a class with him, do it.

Dr. Carleton is very kind and tries to make the class interactive by asking students to answer the questions and there’s an activity once a week where you work with others. Her lectures are recorded and she posts the slides with the content. If I didn’t have her at 9am I would’ve gone to class more often lol, but she’s a good professor. She also allows a cheat sheet for exams

Probably one of the best professors i've had. He actually cares about his students and always comes in with a smile, which does more than you think if you're having a stressful day :). I would love to take him again. My advice is don't try and memorize the powerpoints. I would write almost everything on the powerpoint on my reference sheet and it would barley help. This is because he wants you to have a good understanding of overall concepts, rather than trying to memorize a bunch of facts. Great class, if you do the work, it is easy to succeed with Dr. Fletcher!

Would recommend taking Fletcher. He tries to make lecture engaging and is very enthusiastic about the material. For assignments there are a few homeworks, which are challenging but not too difficult, concept checks after every lecture, and the group worksheets done usually once a week or once every two weeks. The exams are very fair and he allows a note sheet for each one. In lecture he also explains the topics beyond just what is written on the slides and records his lectures which is very helpful for studying. Great teacher!

dr. fletcher is so sweet!! he's an amazing professor and really explains so many concepts very well, making them both interesting and informative. lectures are recorded, there are concept checks and outside pre-work usually once a week (GAEs), and homework is graded for completion. while the slides were dense, they're always easy to come back to and relearn if you don't fully understand or miss a concept during class. the work is very manageable and dr. fletcher is the GOAT!! :D

She is easily one of the best professors I've had so far and potentially one of the best I will ever have. She is not only very experienced with teaching this class but is also genuinely invested in the content and her students. This was the first biology class I had taken in 2 years (AP bio junior year, freshman at the time of writing this) and she made the daunting amount of information in this class extremely manageable and interesting. I will say her lectures are very content packed and we didn't finish all of it every lecture but I think that's just the nature of the class and is difficult to work around. There's also GAE classes which are in-class group activities that essentially force you to make study friends which I really appreciated as I probably wouldn't have gone out of my way to talk to people there otherwise. Her exams are completely fair and not too difficult if you adequately prepare for them and she lets you make cheat sheets for them. She does not curve the class (I don't think it needs too) but she drops the lowest exam, the lowest homework grade, and the lowest GAE score. That said, the homework are for completion, the GAE activity, and the GAE pre-quizes are open note so you'll basically guaranteed to ace them. Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend taking 207 with her.

Dr. Fletcher is amazing. A good person, fair grades (lowest midterm is dropped!), extra credit, and reasonable workload are all things you get with him. Additionally, he encourages questions, is good at explaining topics, and is very welcoming. For the workload, he assigns a short concept check after every lecture, the classes with the group activity have some prep material involved, and there are usually 2-3 homework assignments per midterm, but that's it. For studying, Dr. Fletcher posts an exam guide before every exam that includes some practice exam questions that might even appear on the actual exam. He also allows you to write notes on your equation sheet to use as a reference on the exams. Thank you so much Dr. Fletcher for allowing the reference sheet because there is just so much content covered in BSCI207, I wouldn't even know where to begin studying for it. The exams themselves aren't that hard and they accurately reflect the lecture and GAE material, but there's just a lot of material you have to remember. He also records his lectures which is extremely convenient for note-taking considering the amount of content in this course. The only real downside I can think of is that the final exam is worth more than 1/3 of the final grade, so you really have to study for it. Even then, having this downside is more than worth everything else Dr. Fletcher has to offer.
All his lectures are recorded and he never tests on anything that he didn't cover. Very good teacher who cares about his students. Definitely would take him again.

Dr. Karen was an incredibly kind and intelligent woman, and a great teacher. Regardless, BSCI207 is a very difficult class (at least it was for me - I was a freshman who placed out of BSCI160 & 170, so I jumped straight in). There is SO much content that it gets very overwhelming. She drops one of three midterms, which is very nice though! I found it kind of hard to follow her lectures, but I am not sure if that had anything to do with her or if it's just because the class is hard. She also has office hours in person and on zoom! All lectures are recorded and posted on canvas as well.

Dr. Karen is the nicest professor I have had so far at UMD! She was super accommodating when I got a concussion and had to make up an exam weeks later. She was always so encouraging and gave great, in-depth answers during office hours. A lot of the exam questions pull from the homeworks, GAEs, and concept checks so doing/reviewing those is a great way to study. She drops the lowest exam of 3 and also gives some extra credit. Her final was very fair and I was able to guess most of the topics that would appear. Her lectures are very dense material wise so I would definitely look over them afterwards to make sure you know what's happening in each one. Take her!

Dr. Fletcher is a great professor and he makes it very easy to succeed in his class! If you put in just a little bit of time (which I didn't do and still ended up with a B+) you can totally get an A. A decent amount of stuff is graded for completion and one exam is dropped. I always enjoy having him as a professor and he really wants to see all of his students succeed.

Dr. Karen is one of the professors who wants students to actually learn and appreciate the wonders of the content. BSCI207 was a bumpy but enjoyable ride despite the absolute whirlwind of information. However, Dr. Karen accommodates that by providing everything you possibly need to succeed in this course, from providing practice questions, recording lectures, and having office hours online to allowing a cheat sheet for every exam! She even drops the lowest midterm and provides extra credit opportunities twice in the semester. Homework and GAEs are basically exam preps and graded for completion. However, still put the effort in and compare with answer keys to test your understanding. Although lectures were a little hard to follow, Dr. Karen is still one of the best professors at UMD I've had so far. She genuinely cares about what she's teaching and her students.

Dr. Karen is the sweetest professor, who is extremely passionate about what she teaches and cares about her students a lot. I really enjoyed when she included a bit of outside information that connected to the topics and found it very interesting. The lectures are packed with information, so I would highly recommend rewatching the lectures to ensure understanding of all content. However, all the material needed for the midterms and exams is covered by the GAEs and lectures. The homework and GAEs are basically completion and still the lowest HW and GAE scores are dropped, same with the lowest midterm score. Also, a cheat sheet was allowed for each midterm, which really helped consolidate certain information. Overall, I really enjoyed Dr. Karen as a professor and the class.

I'll start by saying Dr. Shofner is very nice and cares about her students, but that doesn't make up for how unorganized this class is. My class is online and is supposed to be asynchronous with prerecorded lectures and optional question sessions on Zoom every Monday and Wednesday which also serve as her office hours, but very little effort is put into making this class. For the last 4 slide presentations, she hasn't posted the lecture videos (which she explicitly said she will post for all of the slides). There are just slides on new material. Some have just diagrams, but there is no explanation. I signed up for this class knowing there would be video lectures, but now there aren't. Dr. Shofner also doesn't show up to her two day a week office hours/question sessions sometimes with 0 notice or sometimes she will show up 20 minutes late when they are only 50 minutes long. I know professors deal with stuff in their personal lives too, but for the amount of money I had to work for to pay to take this course it is not fair.

Okay so if you're pre-med or any type of pre-health this is going to be the least interesting class you take. Don't get me wrong, Dr. Fletcher is a great professor and you can tell that he really cares about what he's teaching. But oh my god it was so hard for me to care about things like the evolution of fungi. All of his assignments outside of class are easy, take little to no time or can be found on quizlet/coursehero. His exams are fair but theres just so much content to cover. The best advice I can give is to study a little bit after every lecture. If you're able to get access to his past exams you are GOLDEN. Most questions he will use are either exactly the same or some kind of re-work (especially for multiple choice) so you get a really good idea of what information he will want you to get out of it. Overall he's a great guy but if you have poor executive function and need to find things interesting to feel motivated to study them, good luck. I ONLY SAY THIS FOR 207 THOUGH. I also had him for 170, and that class was a delight to take with him.

I took this online during Spring. It was once a week and even for an online this was incredibly disorganized. Just an overflow of information with not real foundation, just jumping from topic to topic. You are also graded on group work, which due to my class being online made it a little difficult to get organized with your team members. Overall I was lucky that it was online, but just the lack of organization made this class unfun.

Dr. Karen is honestly the best professor I’ve had my freshman year. BSCI207 has a lot of content and memorization, but Dr. Karen makes it very palatable. The group activities (GAEs) are very helpful for learning the content and she lets us have a one-page cheat sheet on exams. The lowest midterm, homework, and GAE are dropped. This class does require a lot of effort and studying (review the GAEs and homeworks), but I strongly believe Dr. Karen makes it more enjoyable for us.

Dr. Shofner is a sweet woman but oh my god this class was a DISASTER. I took it online and it was incredibly disorganized. Half the time she wouldn't show up to the weekly zooms and when she did she would ramble on about unrelated topics and basically just repeat everything that was in the recorded lecture. The lectures were supposed to be 50 min, 2 per week however they would end up being closer to an 1 hour 15 min and there would be multiple per day. Sometimes she would just not post a lecture though which I assumed meant she was giving us the day off, then later post it right before the test and say the material covered would be on it. The material on the tests was not at all reflective of what was covered in the lecture and the TAs were incredibly strict about giving partial credit. The tests are also poorly written and many of the questions made no sense. And I know this part has nothing to do with her but the class is just so stupid the information is useless and not applicable to most bio majors.

Yes, this is hard class, but Dr. Karen is a great teacher and really cares about her students. She gives you lots of resources that you will find useful for studying: GAEs, concept checks, homework, etc. She is passionate about bio and puts effort into making class fun when she can. She has been my favorite freshman professor.

Took this class as a junior because I was starting a microbio double major and this class was so easy.
For freshman I imagine this course would be more difficult since it's a lot a lot of content. But the class is structured nicely.
There are 3 midterms and one is dropped. The final exam is based on the last 10 lectures + the content that was covered in the first 3 exams (she said we should only study to make sure we knew what was on the exams, and she provides all exams + keys afterwards).

Attendance is not required and all lectures are recorded. The exception is that there are 11 in-class activities that you should attend as 10 count for a grade. They are super easy though as it asks you to discuss questions with classmates. In these in-class activities, there were a lot of real-life examples that made it very engaging. 
She is very nice! During in-class activities she is understanding and if students say the wrong thing in discussion (in front of the whole class) she'll do her best to reword it such that it works or coach the student to achieve the right answer.

Dr Karen is probably one of the best professors I could've taken as a freshman, I found it hard adapting to her teaching style at the beginning but I still ended up getting an 85% on her first test. I did go to GSS and made sure to study quite a bit, but she also drops the lowest midterm which is nice. I got an 85%, 90%, and 85% on the 3 midterms in order, and with all my hw's and gae's im sitting at a 95% in the class. On midterms you get a whole side of a letter paper to put whatever you want on. Sometimes she even allows both sides! Please take her if you are coming into BSCI 207 as a freshman or any other year, BEST TREACHER EVER!

The only things that I would like to mention is that her class isnt the type where you write everything down, she focuses on concepts and main ideas. Throughout her lectures you'll like automatically understand what shes focusing on and its almost guaranteed to be on the exam. He lectures are on average like 60 to 70 slides so it is not worth it to write everything down. Focus on main ideas and her gae's. Also GSS for this class is a MUST, for us our gss leader posted her worksheets and answer keys so it was nice.
Very nice, can tell she is very passionate about biology, easy grading, GAEs are helpful enough, fast paced but if you study enough you should be fine, you should take her if available

Dr. Carleton is super passionate about biology. She allows drops of some assignments (I forget how many) and 1 exam. I would say the content is a lot, as any other biology course, but it should be fine to learn if you study and commit time to the class. She records her lectures which was super helpful. It's super helpful to me because I rewrite and complete details into my notes that I might have missed in lecture. She is very kind, generous, and always hoping to make the class fun by making the class interactive. I would recommend her!

I would 100% recommend Dr. Carleton (She tells us to call her Dr. Karen instead) especially if you are a freshman. She is extremely kind, she caters to different issues you may have, and is honestly one of the best professors I've had. In terms of the course, we have 3 midterms, 11 HWs which are honestly free points as they are graded on effort, not whether you got the Q right, and 11 GAE quizzes which are online (She drops the lowest one of each). You also get a cheat sheet for all exams including the final. Overall 207 is a very challenging course but she made it passable.

Dr. Fletcher is such a good professor! His lectures are always recorded so you can watch them anytime, but I highly recommend attending lectures so you can ask questions. My favorite part of the class is the GAEs because you get points for simply trying, same with the homework. You do have post lecture quizzes but they are very easy and you get 3 tries unlimited time. The pre-GAEs are a bit harder because you have to do the reading to understand and you only get 1 attempt. But he drops your lowest GAE, pre-GAE, homework, post-lecture quiz, and exam (excluding the final). You get cheat sheets on your exam, one page (only the front) of hand written notes. The exams are all 75 points. If you put in the effort and ask questions, you'll be alright. I went to office hours once, and I still did pretty good in the class.

Dr. Fletcher is probably the best professor I had this semester. He records his lectures and drops the lowest exam, homework, and GAE. His exams are pretty fair/easy, and I got at least an 80 on both the first 2 exams. On the third, I woke up late and had 20 minutes to take a 50 minute exam, which was unfortunate but again, he drops the lowest exam. He is so nice and truly cares about his students. Definitely recommend him for any Bio class.

Dr. Carleton is a great professor, she really cares about her students and makes an effort to promote true learning and application of concepts instead of memorization throughout a very difficult course. She provided a lot of resources like practice quizzes (concept checks) and her office hours were very helpful.

Such a nice woman, very dedicated to her craft and her students' well being. 207 isn't egregiously hard, but make sure to study all her supplemental stuff on ELMS to get the best possible understanding of the content. She also allows note sheets during exams which was great!

PLS take her she is one the best BSCI professors out there, she is very caring and teaches the information very well. For such a hard class she makes her exams really fair and so if you studied you will be fine. Most of our assignments were bases on completion except for the exams and GAE quizzes which were online. Overall, this class was really enjoyable and taking it with her is very rewarding

Dr. Karen was a wonderful professor. The class overall was difficult due to the large amount of information being tested. Additionally, the class was not only included biology, but also included subjects like mathematics, physics, and biochemistry, though it was minimal. It took a very holistic approach to organismal biology, including all angles towards the topic. But Dr. Karen tried to make it as digestible as possible. She included a lot of sample problems through check-in quizzes (that weren't graded). A few of those questions even popped up on the final surprisingly. Additionally, she dropped one of the midterms and quizzes, allowing for some leeway. For the final, she doesn't make you review all the content. Instead, she only tests you on the material that was previously tested on the midterms (at least that is how she did it for our semester). This means you don't need to study everything taught during the whole semester, which is fantastic. She also allowed cheat sheets on each exam, so some of the more hyperspecific material did not need to be memorized. Overall, I would definitely recommend Dr. Karen for this class. She explained all the topics thoroughly - making sure there was no confusion - and she always tried her best to help.

Honestly one of the best professors at umd. PLS take her she is so caring and kind. She actually wants to teach biology and make sure that every student understands. she has around 11 hws which are all completion and GAE which are also for completion. Her exams are fair but hard, If you study than you will be fine. Overall i loved her teaching style and she is very approachable for office hours.

Fletcher is a great professor. He records all his lectures and uploads them to Canvas, so really, the only time you have to attend class is when he hosts Group Activity assignments during class (GAEs). You will get full points on the homework and in-class GAEs for just attempting them. The online concept checks have three attempts and unlimited time, while the online GAE-preps have one attempt with unlimited time. He does ramble a bit during lectures but usually gets through everything he needs to just fine. You do get cheat sheets for all the exams, the front page of the equation sheet for all the midterms, and the front and back of the equation sheet for the final exam. I would have done better if I studied more, so just study a decent amount and write what you can't grasp onto the cheat sheet and you'll be fine. He also rounds up grades, my 86.45% was rounded up to an 87% for a B+.

Dr. Fletcher is a great person, very friendly and approachable. This class is a LOT of content, you were expected to know specific lineages of random animals and random facts. This class built on previous bio classes so you needed to have background knowledge because he doesn't explain basics like cellular respiration. I actually had no clue how to study for this class as it is purely memorization although he does let you have a cheat sheet (1-sided). I recommend the GSS worksheets, they were like recaps. The GAE (group activities) and homework were graded on completion so that did help with my grade a bit. The recorded lectures were really helpful because the lectures were packed with content so if you missed something, you can always look back on it. He drops one exam score and one assignment from each category. I thought the 2nd unit was the toughest because it was very very specific, you either know it or you don't. The final wasn't too hard, it was about 50% new content and 50% old content. Overall this is probably the most boring biology class I've taken but Dr. Fletcher made it bearable.

Dr. Carleton is one of the best BSCI 207 professors here at UMD. While this class is challenging and requires a LOT of studying outside of class, Dr. Carleton makes the information easy to apply and understand. The GAEs and homework are especially helpful when studying for exams, and the lowest midterm, GAE, and homework grade are all dropped. Overall, this class, while having a ton of information, is very manageable if you are willing to put in the effort (attend office hours, go to GSS, take detailed notes in class, etc.). Dr. Carleton genuinely cares about her students and is dedicated to making sure you take something significant away from the class, and is very knowledgeable about a wide range of biology topics. She is incredibly sweet, and you can tell she enjoys teaching this class.

Would highly recommend taking Dr. Karen. She is super nice, passionate, and caring. Her teaching style is also pretty good and she always records her lectures. Her midterms are always very fair and also have application based questions which is surprising for a biology class. She also drops the lowest scoring midterm. In terms of assignments, its not much work at all with just 11 HWs and 11 short quizzes before GAEs. I know a lot of people who don't even show up to lecture and still do fine. Sometimes I felt that the course content was useless for me, especially Unit 2 which is almost memorization, but Dr. Karen made it manageable. The TAs are also pretty helpful in GAE sometimes. A great professor to take this class if you have to. The class is more based on knowing concepts then memorization, so make sure to get the general gist of things before the midterm.

As a freshman, I was pretty nervous about being in STEM classes at UMD since I've heard some profs who do research are a lot less dedicated to teaching. However, Dr. Karen is definitely the best bio prof I could have taken. She is genuinely so kind and truly has a passion for teaching students biology. Her lectures are very organized, and the way she teaches is easy to understand. Her office hours are also really approachable so I felt encouraged to go to them and ask questions. As for work, there's around 11 hwks and GAE which are all graded based on completion. There are 3 midterms and a final, and your lowest midterm grade gets dropped. The exams themselves are difficult but fair. As long as you study and make a comprehensive "cheat-sheet" (she allows a single/double page cheat sheet each exam), you'll be fine. To summarize, DEFINITELY TAKE HER IF U CAN!!!

Honest she was a very boring professor which made it hard to really focus in her lectures. She record her lectures and post the slides. Her GAE are crucial for exams especially for the FRQ portion. Her midterms were ok but the final was a bit unreasonable. Overall not the greatest experience.

She is amazing! Dr. Karen is so sweet and an awesome professor. She is funny, empathetic, and passionate about what she teaches. Bio is a challenging subject in general, with a lot of information, but Dr. Karen really sets you up for success. She gives you every resource you need to do well on exams, it just depends on how much time you dedicate to studying. I learned that the best method was quick notes in class, then rewatching the recorded lectures the next day/taking notes to really help the information stick (prevents cramming before exams). I would highly recommend her!

Fletcher is a solid professor and is very friendly and open to questions during office hours. All lectures are recorded and he posts the slides on Canvas. There are 3 exams that cover the first 3 units and the final exam which is cumulative. He splits the exams 50/50 with multiple choice and short answer. Overall, the exams are fair as the questions come in a very similar format to other assignments. These assignments consist of homework, concept checks, and GAEs (group classwork). Homework and GAEs are graded for completion and concepts checks have multiple attempts. I recommend completing all these as they make studying a lot easier and he drops the lowest for each assignment type including the lowest of the 3 exams. He also posts exam guides which contains questions that are on the exam itself. <2 hr work per week outside of class besides studying. Course content is well organized but also very broad. Great professor overall and I would recommend him for 207.

Dr. Karen is a great professor but the class is useless. Please do NOT take this class if it isn’t a requirement. I don’t know why as a microbiology major I was required to take this class. Don’t even understand the point of learning about all these crazy animals (e.g. stramenopiles) and these ancient periods?? Felt like I was in a history class. This class should be a requirement for an animal science major only. I gave three stars because Dr. Karen is sweet and approachable. Her exams are hard though. I don’t know how she said the class is doing “good”, when the average was 52/75!!
Super nice, helpful, explains very in depth in office hours, understanding and overall amazing person!

Dr. G is incredibly kind and a great professor. Her lectures are interesting and exams and assignments in the class are perfectly fair. Be warned that if you take her lecture, you have to socially interact with people about once a week in lecture hall, but it's not so bad. Overall totally recommend for 207. As for the class itself, it's really quite easy. It just contains massive amounts of information that you have to know. There isn't a lot of hard thinking and there are no puzzles or tricks, it's really more like listening to a long story.
His review packets are very helpful

Carleton is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. I love her as a professor. With that being said, BSCI207 was pretty heinous. I gave up on learning anything and just fit all the lectures on my cheat sheet for my exams. The class itself was interesting, but it was just information overload. Don't take 207 unless you have to.

took this class last sem, and carleton is a great prof. her slideshows are very easy to read and get information from. she gives a decent amount of examples, but not too much. tests weren't bad and pretty easy to do good. the cheat sheet was helpful for studying but I barely used it on the actual test. some of the material from 207 is boring and not very applicable to life, but if you can get over that it's a chill and fun class. i'd highly recommend taking her

Dr. Carleton is a pretty good professor and is very sweet. Her class isn't too hard but the content isn't very useful to other classes. She allows you to bring a cheat sheet to exams which is very helpful and she sometimes gets bored of the content she's teaching and you can tell, would definitely recommend her though.

Dr. G is so sweet and helpful. The content covered in 207 was definitely not my favorite, but Dr. G honestly made the class bearable. The midterms usually cover 7 lectures and 3 GAE's -- the content is A LOT. I suggest going to office hours because she usually explains topics and it's much more digestible then. She will also not include stupid small things on the midterms, like how does this protist move etc., because she isn't trying to test how well you memorized the content; rather, she is testing how well you understand it. There are 11 homeworks in total, and yes, some are really confusing, but she will literally go through it with you in office hours. The GAEs are very easy too, she doesn't actually want you to submit a worksheet, instead it's a Google form you fill out at the end so she can gauge how well the class understood the content. I highly suggest taking her for 207 because she was a student not too long ago and she knows how we feel as students!

DO NOT TAKE HER. Lectures seem fine until the exam where they are extremely hard. All the GAE’s and HW you do BARELY boosts your grade. This class should not have been as hard as it was and I blame it all on her teaching. The exams are HARDER THAN THEY SHOULD BE and super specific considering in class you play with pipe cleaners….

She's a good teacher and cares about her students. The class material isn't my favorite, but she makes it more interesting. There are 3 midterms, each covering 10 lectures. She lets us have cheat sheets for each exam because there's A LOT of material. The exams can be challenging, but she doesn't word things weirdly or anything. She provides us with questions at the end of each lecture that, when put together, create a great study guide for her exams. I liked taking her, and would suggest her to other students.

Dr. Carleton is an amazing professor who explains concepts clearly and really knows the material. However, the class itself is very boring, and a lot of the content—especially in Unit 2—feels pointless. The homework assignments don’t add much value either. This class is only worth taking if it’s a major requirement. That said, it’s fairly easy to do well. Dr. Carleton allows a cheat sheet on the exams, which are fair and closely reflect the lectures, quizzes, and GAE assignments (which are basically the FRQs on the tests). I usually skipped the in-person lectures, watched the recordings on 2x speed, and completed the quizzes while taking notes on key points and any missed questions. Writing out the cheat sheet by hand helped solidify the material and made studying more effective.

Teacher lowkey yaps a lot and her slides are 50-60 slides every lecture, giving you a minute to jot notes or else you’re screwed and left behind in the dust. Course is super unclear and has way too much content, making every test just confusing and you’ll end up studying everything BUT the stuff on the test. Karlton also just praises her colleagues too much and even puts their ideas on exams despite it not even being published. You’re basically tested on her friends lol. She’s a nice person but not a good teacher. Don’t take her if you can’t focus and lock in well. Most of the learning will be done outside of class.

bsci207 is overall a pointless course, DONT TAKE it if its not required for your major. that being said, carleton makes it pretty manageable by posting her slideshows and recording her lectures, and she is very helpful during office hours. however i honestly think her lectures are not engaging, and she sometimes spends way too much time going over things that are irrelevant and wont be on the exam. overall her lectures are overwhelming and she goes way too fast on some things, but i guess thats bound to happen when all her slideshows are 50+ slides.

The class itself is inbetween bsci170 and bsci160, so it focuses on organisms and like how they evolved and function. Dr. Carleton is very nice but her lectures are very boring. If you do go to lecture, I would recommend sitting in the front because you will not be able to pay attention in the back (also kind of hard to hear her clearly/focus on whats shes saying). She does record her lectures and I found those super helpful when studying, but I would recommend staying ontop of the lectures and attending class to get a stronger understanding of the topics rather than cram before the exam. The first exam is definitely the hardest, but the second and third one are more fair. She does allow cheat sheets on the exams, which is definitely necessary when it comes to all the content.
Good, just a lot of content that is covered. Helps if your friends come to class to keep you motivated as well. Carleton keeps her classes moderately engaging

This course is really boring and useless. Carleton herself has told us she thinks it's pointless and that it is basically a repeat of 160 and 170. As a lecturer, she has a very documentary kind of voice so it is hard to stay focused. Her slides can also be kind of confusing because they will say so much and yet so little at the same time. She plans these activities called GAEs about once a week that were really unhelpful. They were supposed to help us apply the concepts but they felt stupid and didn't really help me or my friends. I think she is a really nice lady and she definitely cares about her students. I also appreciate that she posts the lecture recordings because it makes it a good class to skip. My only problem with her as a professor was that I disliked the course more than I liked her.

Carleton is one of the sweetest professors I have had. It is clear she cares about her students and wants to help everyone do well.
In terms of the class, it is pretty straightforward, there is a lot of stuff to learn but most of it isn't super hard so it wasn't too bad. She gives you a lot of small easy ways to bring your grade up, and makes it clear she cares more about general understanding than getting everything perfect. As long as you keep up and come to class its not bad. Carleton's lectures can be a bit dull but she tries to make them interesting and connect the material to stuff you know.

Took BSCI207 as a first semester freshman coming in with AP Bio credit. I think Dr. Carleton started the first lecture with hard math to scare people or something but it got easier after the first week. The course is a mixture of rote memorization and applying basic math. 

Grades are a homework worksheet (completion) every week or so, a few pre-GAE quizzes that are easy if you watched/read the prep, GAE attendance (approx once a week or less), and 3 exams and the final. With the padding, it’s not hard to get an A or B as long as you do okay on exams, which you’re allowed to have a page of handwritten notes for. The questions basically come off of the slides and GAEs, so if you pay attention to lectures and bring a note sheet you’ll be fine. All lectures are recorded and PPTS are posted before the lecture.

 Dr. Carleton is clearly very knowledgeable about the subject and is a really sweet person. She has slides with the basic info you need but always has extra fun facts and book recommendations. She tries to engage with the class but no one wants to answer her questions or ask any so it’s a little bit sad. I like her a lot though and she seems really chill and cares about her students.

Sweetest professor ever. The class itself seems pretty boring/useless info but i mean that's not her fault. She does her best to make it interesting and enjoyable. She records lectures if you miss which is really nice, and posts the lectures too. First exam was rough and much more challenging than the other 2. Content itself isnt challenging conceptually, what got me was some of the super specific multiple choice that I sometimes felt was unfair because it wasn't a true reflection of understanding the content, just annoying memorization. Exam 2 is the most annoying just because it was SOOOO much useless info, but make a good cheat sheet and you will b fine. Didnt attend GSS because again, the concepts were bad it was just multiple choice that got me. I have a 92 right now, but Im expecting the final to potentially be rough just because of those useless multiple choice questions. Also the GAE's are a hit or miss, sometimes they help and sometimes its just useless but hey its free points.

Honestly, Carleton is a nice professor. She seems like she cares about her students and is very approachable. But this class is literally just a bunch of random facts and information spit at you. Her lectures are pretty boring and she's very monotone but goes super fast so it's hard to keep up/stay focused. I stopped coming to lectures and started watching the lecture panopto videos, which was helpful. The exams are no where near as detailed as the info in her lectures which makes it hard to study because you can never really tell what will be on the exam. She does let you have cheat sheets but most of the time, unless I put literally every single thing on the cheatsheet, I barely use it. If you can take any other bio class, do that.

I wouldn’t take this class unless you really need to. There’s an intense amount of content, and it’s not just memorization, you have to actually understand it well enough to apply it to new situations on the exams. Also, ignore older reviews saying you can drop an exam, I took the course fall 2025, and that was no longer an option. That said, Dr. Carleton is genuinely very kind and responsive over email. She clearly wants students to succeed and is a great person overall. The lectures are recorded, but they’re very information-heavy, so I personally found it much easier to watch them on my own time and pause to take thorough notes. There are graded in-class activities where you get full credit just for showing up, and the homework is completion-based, which helps balance things out. The real challenge is the exams, there’s no test bank, and the in-class activities don’t really prepare you for the free-response questions. Still, if you put in the time to study, you can definitely do okay.

He is an amazing teacher! He is a very nice guy and very approachable. All of his exams are very fair and he also provides a lot of homework and extra opportunities to do well in the class. I would suggest doing all of the concept checks and reviewing the GAE's before the exams as a lot of the questions are the same. The only thing negative I have to say about him is that in class he can go through his slides very fast sometimes making it somewhat hard to keep up in class. However, he does record all of his lectures and posts all of his slides so this is really a non issue. Great guy and its very obvious he has a lot of passion. Shoutout Dr. Fletcher!!!

I would not recommend, her lectures are pretty boring with 60+ slides per lecture, and she has a monotone voice that makes them very hard to follow. The exam questions can be any small thing from the lectures, which each have countless seemingly irrelevant facts, and the homework assignments are always confusing and vague. Thankfully we got cheat sheets for each exam, so going through each lecture and writing notes onto my sheet before each exam gave me an A, but the class overall just frustrated me and I would take a different teacher if possible.

Dr Fletcher is an amazing professor! BSCI207 has a lot of content but he always tries to explain it in a way that makes sense. His test are very fair and you get a sheet of notes for each test. He also always had an extra point on his exams (even the final) and it was something really easy. If you have the opportunity to take Dr Fletcher I definitely would!
Great professor. She is a bit fast going through slides but she is a wonderful person and great professor. Her final is pretty hard compared to the midterms so keep that in mind.

Dr. Karen was nice and helpful, but I'm not gonna lie this was one of my least favorite classes (and I usually love biology). The lectures were long (usually 60 slides) and the things on the slide were different from what she was saying (so you have to pay attention to both). Halfway through the semester, I stopped attending because she records the lectures and I just started watching those. DO NOT take notes from scratch, it is wayy too much work. Highly recommend using an ipad and importing the slides into a notetaking app like goodnotes for annotations. She doesn't give any practice tests or extra material for the test, but she does allow a cheat sheet. It is a good way to study because you can condense and organize all the material. If you write small and highlight, you can get a lot out of the cheat sheet. The tests were a lot easier than I thought as long as you spend the time studying before. The material tho was very much memorization based and all the units felt very disconnected, which made it harder to study for the final. Overall, a very heavy class but you should be able to manage if you are willing to put a lot of work in.

He is so kind and caring. His lectures may seem boring sometimes, but he explains the concepts thoroughly and makes sure that you understand and is open to questions during class. The exams are pretty straightforward despite being just a dense course on mostly facts. Make sure to know the concepts and examples given in class even if you do not know the itty bitty details. If you have questions, there are always office hours where he is open to helping you out. The other grades like the GAEs, concept checks, and homeworks (completion grades) are easy to score good points on if you just pay attention to the material provided, its also not too much work. The class is not curved, but if you just put good effort into the semester, and remember the facts (a lot of memorizing) you should be able to get a good grade overall. No

Genuinely one of the nicest and sweetest people I've seen at UMD, and an alright class overall. There's a lot of information covered in BSCI207, and she doesn't expect you to memorize it all, mostly just the general knowledge and idea. You do get a cheat sheet for each exam, longer units having a double-sided sheet (handwritten). Once again, she really wants you to succeed, and you should pay attention to the GAEs and review them for the free response. Exams aren't exactly easy because of the sheer amount of content, but it's doable if you review.  There's no curve or exam drop like I've seen happen before, but we had three exams, and the final unit was 50% of the final.

I took Dr. Fletcher for both BSCI170 and BSCI207 and he rocks !! Very fair exams that can be studied for easily by reviewing course materials and his practice questions. He’s very responsive and approachable, and is clearly so smart and an engaging lecturer even when teaching subjects that involve tons of info. Also super helpful that all of his lectures are recorded and you’ll always know well ahead of time if there will be a graded in-class group activity

I loved Dr. Carleton. Genuinely just a kind person with a very calming presence and voice. The class itself is a bit of an information dump, there's like a 50+ slideshow every class but she posts them all along with recordings and you get a cheatsheet on every test including the final. The midterms are 20 mcq with 3 frqs, she doesn't post practice exams but I think they reflect what's in class well. The only test I did bad on was exam 1 because the frqs were kind of random and worded confusing imo but that was also my first college exam ever so it may not be her fault. The rest of the exams were very manageable and much better. Overall, I would recommend her I thought she was a great professor.

The class and prof are extremely fair. Study and you'll be fine. Go to office hours, she writes down a list of kids she (supposedly..) bumps the grades up for if they're on the edge at the end of the sem. It can be kind of a lot of pointless content but again, she's fair about it; if everyone does bad on a certain question or concept bc it's too obscure she'll curve that one part. Generally though, there's no curve, no tests dropped, but you get a cheat sheet. About the prof though, Dr. Karen is genuinely extremely nice and sweet and I loved her so much, I'll miss her.

Carleton is a really nice professor, and I love that she records the lectures. You don't need to go to class as long as you watch lecture recordings. The class absolutely sucks, but if you're a bio major, you have to take it. Tests are based on the content she talks about. Frqs are based on GAEs. There is a small curve at the end, which can round your grade up.

Great prof, she's super sweet and fair. Midterms are only worth 65 pts, with the final being worth 125 pts. Homework is basically just based on participation. Lecture is a little slow and boring, but I wouldn't say its the most interesting class anyways (imo). I'd recommend looking over the key concepts at the end of each lecture since she bases her exams on those questions. The concept checks are also pretty helpful. Overall, I'd highly recommend Dr. K

As much as the class is difficult, Dr. Carleton is extremely nice. If you are a first semester freshman taking this class as I was, do not underestimate the first exam and be sure to take your time writing good notes during lecture. (I prefer using a google doc/typing, I used an iPad first unit and there was too much material and lecture went to quick to write quality notes) Expect that this class will take a lot of studying, but if you do it you will do well.

Absolutely love Dr. Fletcher!!! He is such an amazing professor and is truly passionate about what he does. He is also genuinely one of the nicest professors I have ever met at UMD. He makes the content easy to understand and his exams are very fair. Would definitely recommend taking him!

She clearly wants students to succeed and is a great person overall. The lectures are recorded, but they’re very information-heavy, so I personally found it much easier to watch them on my own time and pause to take thorough notes. There are graded in-class activities where you get full credit just for showing up, and the homework is completion-based, which helps balance things out. The real challenge is the exams, there’s no test bank, and the in-class activities don’t really prepare you for the free-response questions. Still, if you put in the time to study, you can definitely do okay.

Dr. Carleton is super sweet and she genuinely cares about her students. I just found these topics to be very boring and I had a hard time paying attention, since there aren't a lot of concepts- its more of "this plant is different than that plant which is the same as this other plant" which can be very dull. The cheat sheets are genius, she doesn't drop exams anymore, and homework is basically completion. the lectures can be very fast (60 slides in 50 minutes) and you really don't need all the info she gives. i'd recommend going back through the lectures and writing down the key things. memorize the concept checks, homework, and GAE's and you'll be okay! i thought the first midterm was really hard (but to be fair it was also my first ever exam in college) + the 2nd + 3rd midterms were both doable and pretty easy! bring an energy drink to class!

Dr. Karen is one of the sweetest and most knowledgeable professors out there. While the content of this class was one of the most inapplicable (especially unit 2) to pre-med content, if you can ignore that it will be fine. 

The other reviews were not lying when they said this class is like drinking out of a fire hose. But med school is also like drinking out of a fire hose, so this class is a perfect way to learn to use Anki before it matters (for the MCAT or med school). 

Dr. Karen genuinely cares about her students. Once I was confused on how to study and she scheduled a one on one meeting with me. She discussed study methods really well. Just look at the key questions and you will be fine.

Dr. Karen is a very sweet professor who is clearly passionate about what she is teaching. I found the first two units to be a bit dull but the last units were very interesting. Her lectures have A LOT of slides with A LOT of information making it challenging to take thorough notes during class. However, going through the concept checks and reading through the slideshows after class and before tests helped me retain the information. The midterms and final were very fair in my opinion and she allows you to have a cheat sheet for each test.

I love Dr. Carleton. Not only is she super sweet, but she's insanely knowledgeable and clearly understands every word on her slides. She is very wordy, though! And her voice is a little soft, but I personally really like her inflections. It's like Blues Clues, or some other kids show... very gentle and guiding. If you're not already a little well-versed in the bio world, it might be a little hard to keep up. Usually she reads a bit of what's on the slides, then talks about it more without reading off the slide. It can be a little fast! However, not everything she says needs to be noted, and she often stops to ask the class questions and is receptive to being asked questions herself. She posts all of her slides, notes, and recordings, regardless of if it was a lecture day or GAE (groupwork) day. I will say, the few lectures I missed felt hard to catch up on, and DONT sleep on exams. She lets you have a cheat-sheet where you can write whatever you want to keep in mind, but don't think one exam will be too easy to fully prepare for. That's what cost me my A! The TAs were very helpful when it came to prep, one of them ran review sessions once a week and posted practice questions for exams. Don't cram, give yourself lots of time to fully absorb all the info. It can really be a lot, but if you talk to her, she'll help lay everything out and show you what you should and shouldn't focus on. You can also email her about anything and she'll always respond within a few days.

Not entirely related, but she also does a lot of research on cichlids and vision, which is super cool!

I took this class fall of 2025 and Dr. Carleton is such a sweet and understanding professor. The course is fairly graded and the resources like the concept checks, GAE worksheets, and GSS sheets provided by the TAs are super helpful. There is definitely a lot of content to learn so I would study in advance by a few days and sit in the front if you for attention span’s sake. The key concepts for lectures are super helpful and this class is doable for sure. The workload isn’t too much and the HWs are helpful to make sense of lecture info and as guides for exam written response questions. Would highly recommend Dr. K for this course!

Dr. Karen genuinely cares about her students and their success in this class. While I disagree with the fact that this class is a major requirement for bio she still made it very interesting and worthwhile. She records all of the lectures if you can't make it, although I would recommend going because watching the Panopto's can become tedious when you cram them. Her exams aren't necessarily easy but if you do the things she recommends and take advantage of the extra resources it is very possible to get an A or even an A+. I very much recommend taking Dr. Carleton for this class.

Took this course as a freshman which was maybe a bad idea, but the professor was great. She's very sweet and helpful, although one critique I had was that lectures kind of felt all over the place (50-60 slides, sometimes with very little correlation) and she went a little fast for me. Exams were tricky but overall pretty fair, and as long as you go to lectures (or at least actually watch the recordings) you should be ok. I got a little sloppy with my attendance towards the end and it definitely showed, but even then office hours and the TAs were all pretty helpful tools.
